args.query: NVIDIA executive leadership CEO Jensen Huang official bio

observations.content:
Summary: Jensen Huang, born February 17, 1963, in Tainan, Taiwan, is a Taiwanese-born American entrepreneur who cofounded the American semiconductor company NVIDIA Corporation in 1993. He serves as the company's president, chief executive officer, and a member of the board of directors. Huang holds a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering from Oregon State University and a master’s degree in electrical engineering from Stanford University. Under his leadership, NVIDIA has become a leading provider of graphics processing units (GPUs) and a key player in the artificial intelligence boom. Huang has been elected to the National Academy of Engineering and appointed to the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology in 2026.

[1] Jensen Huang | Biography, NVIDIA, Huang’s Law, & Facts | Britannica Money
    https://www.britannica.com/money/Jensen-Huang
    Jensen Huang (born February 17, 1963, Tainan, Taiwan) is a Taiwanese-born American entrepreneur who cofounded the American semiconductor company NVIDIA Corporation. Under Huang’s leadership, NVIDIA has become one of the leading providers of graphics processing units (GPUs) and has taken center stage in the current artificial intelligence (AI) boom. [...] In April 1993 Huang founded NVIDIA with fellow microchip designers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, who selected Huang to serve as CEO. The trio aimed to create GPUs for the video game industry. The trio began with $40,000 in capital but soon procured an initial investment of $20 million from venture capital firms. With this backing, NVIDIA survived a difficult first few years and eventually gained a solid position in the semiconductor market. The company went public in 1999. When its stock [...] Huang graduated with a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering from OSU in 1984. He moved to Silicon Valley, where he took a job with Advanced Micro Devices. He remained there for about a year before accepting a job at the LSI Logic Corporation, where he rose through the ranks and eventually became director of a company division. While working, he returned to school and obtained a master’s degree in electrical engineering from Stanford University.
